#    Nodes per native model pixel. The model works at 30 m, so this sets both
#    the size of the world and what a node means. Vertical scale follows it, so
#    terrain is never stretched, and changing it does not need a rebake because
#    the tile cache is stored at the model's own resolution.
#
#      1   30 m per node    1860 km world
#      4   7.5 m per node    465 km world
#     30   1 m per node       62 km world
#
#    Thirty is the one where the rest of the game works. Everything Luanti and
#    its games size in nodes, a cave passage, a tree, a doorway, assumes a node
#    is about a metre, and at 7.5 m per node all of it comes out seven times too
#    big. At 1 m per node the world is only 62 km across, which is the whole of
#    Luanti's map, and Everest would still fit inside the height limit.
tdl_nodes_per_pixel (Nodes per native pixel) int 30 1 30

#    Y coordinate of sea level.
tdl_sea_level (Sea level) int 0 -30000 30000

#    Peak roughness added below the model's 30 m sampling, in metres, on the
#    steepest ground. Scaled down by local slope, so plains stay flat. This is
#    the only source of relief finer than 30 m: the model has none.
tdl_detail_metres (Sub pixel detail) float 20.0 0.0 120.0

#    Cave passage scale in metres. Sized in metres rather than nodes, so caves
#    stay the same size in the world whatever the node scale is. A real cave
#    passage is a few metres across, so caves only become worth crawling through
#    once nodes are about a metre.
tdl_cave_size (Cave scale) float 45.0 10.0 500.0

#    How much of the rock is hollow. Zero switches caves off entirely.
tdl_cave_amount (Cave amount) float 0.075 0.0 0.4

#    Sample climate from this many times further out than the terrain. A 62 km
#    world sits inside one climate zone, so an honest one comes out all the same
#    biome. Raising this lets a small world cross the climate gradients of a much
#    larger one, at the cost of weather that does not match the world's size.
#    Elevation, rivers and wetness are unaffected. 1 is honest.
tdl_climate_stretch (Climate stretch) float 1.0 1.0 16.0

#    Degrees colder per kilometre of height. Altitude is the one climate
#    gradient a small world genuinely has, so this is what puts snow on the
#    peaks and forest in the valleys. The real figure is about 6.5.
tdl_lapse_rate (Lapse rate) float 6.0 0.0 15.0

#    How much wetter it gets with height, as a fraction of the rainfall added
#    per two kilometres. Mountains catch the rain the plains behind them miss.
tdl_orographic (Orographic rainfall) float 0.5 0.0 3.0

#    Take the ground nodes from the biomes the game registers, matching this
#    mod's computed temperature and rainfall against their heat and humidity
#    points. Works with any game that registers biomes, which is any game that
#    works with the engine mapgens. Turn it off to use this mod's own node
#    names, which are Mineclonia's.
tdl_use_game_biomes (Use the game's own biomes) bool true
